pr_body:
Remove available property from Kodi that was added in 2022.6 to prevent unavailable status
after shutdown of Kodi box which disables turn_on service

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Remove the `available` property (added in PR #69115) from Kodi as returning False for this property results in the `media_player` entity for Kodi being in the status `unavailable`, which in turn prevents the `media_player.turn_on` service from running on it and it removes the power on button from the media_player cards.
Due to Kodi being "off" meaning there will be no network connection to Kodi itself (as opposed to a running instance of Kodi returning a status of Off), the `available` property should not return `False` when Kodi is unreachable.

issue_context.title: Kodi player power button absent when 'unavailable'
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Kodi media player entity is `unavailable` when Home Assistant starts until the related kodi instance comes online. This prevents the power button from showing up on the media player card.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.6.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.5.5

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Kodi

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/kodi/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

Potentially introduced by [#69115](url=https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/69115)?

Appears similar to issue previously resolved by [#41714](url=https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/41714).

Hey there @onfreund, @cgtobi, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`kodi`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L554) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I don't even only have it at first start. Once Kodi suspends it becomes unavailable again too and thus I can no longer trigger its `turn_on` trigger that will send wake-on-lan packet to get it to resume.

Yeah, this is definitely introduced by https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/69115, reverting that change (essentially removing ```available``` property or making it always return True) resolves this.
Will the integration get updated to fix this newly introduced issue?

Alexanv1 is correct, the addition of the `available` property (at least as it is defined as available if no errors on connection) is what broke this.
Not sure if the `available` property was needed for anything, as the original PR does not specify this, however it definitely breaks at least some systems (I would guess most, however it is possible it's needed for some).
Given this is a pretty big issue for me, I've created a PR to remove that property, though I haven't contributed to HA before and not sure of all the rules, flows, etc so have no idea if the PR will (eventually) be merged, but I want to at least get some traction on it. If someone more experience in HA, or the integration maintaners want to completely create a new PR for this because I missed something or whatever, please do so.

review_comments: We are we firing events from an entity ?

I'm not sure, I just removed the available method as, once the network connection is lost with Kodi, it causes it to go into unavailable, which doesn't work well for Kodi. Is it required for something related to events, shall I put the method back in, but always return `True`? (for reference, the method wasn't there before, then got added with the implementation that I removed so I would imagine it should be fine to remove it instead of returning always `True`)

This is a separate issue.  It really shouldn't work like this, but it does.

Anyways its definitely going to break with adding `available` since you can never turn it on once its unavailable.

Let's revert the change for now.  Hopefully this can be refactored to be a bit more inline with standards in the future.
